players.product: large gas/diesel reciprocating gensets (PGM130, 10 MW medium-speed gas platform) and Solar Turbines gas turbines for data-center prime and backup power

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results: sales and revenues were $17.4 billion, up 22% and in line with expectations; adjusted operating profit margin 18.0% and adjusted profit per share $5.54 (up 30%) were better than anticipated, mainly on favorable manufacturing costs including lower than anticipated tariff costs (about $600 million in the quarter).
quarterly_data.figure: sales $17.4 billion (+22%); adj EPS $5.54; adj op margin 18.0%

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog grew to a record $63 billion, an increase of $28 billion or 79% versus Q1 2025, and 'almost $12 billion sequentially'; all three primary segments contributed; total first-quarter orders were an all-time record. CEO: since the initial capacity expansion plans in January 2024, the large reciprocating engine backlog 'has grown by more than 3.5x', with customers committing to longer-term orders, 'some orders well into 2028'. Multi-year orders typically carry price escalators agreed in frame agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $63 billion (+79%); large recip engine backlog more than 3.5x since January 2024

quarterly_data.signal: Power & Energy: sales to users grew 32% with growth across all applications; power generation driven by strong demand for large gensets and turbines used in data center applications 'with an increasing mix towards prime power'. Segment sales $7.0 billion, up 22%, exceeding expectations on power generation strength; segment margin 20.6% (tariffs about a 270 basis point impact; capacity-expansion spend and higher depreciation also weighed).
quarterly_data.figure: P&E sales $7.0 billion (+22%); margin 20.6%; P&E sales to users +32%

quarterly_data.signal: Announced an opportunity to provide ProPower up to 2.1 GW of large gas generator sets for prime power generation in support of data center, oil and gas and industrial applications; orders enter backlog on a rolling basis, deliveries over the next five years, with long-term services opportunity. This is 'the sixth agreement with at least 1 GW of Caterpillar equipment for prime power applications', plus multiple sub-1 GW prime power projects; having both turbines and recips is an advantage for behind-the-meter sites.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 2.1 GW (ProPower); sixth agreement with at least 1 GW for prime power

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: increasing large reciprocating engine capacity from 2x 2024 levels to nearly 3x 2024 levels (factory output in units), driven mostly by power generation / data-center capex; investment to begin as soon as possible but primarily 2027 through 2029, with incremental units hoped for as early as 2027. CEO estimates it will add 'another 15 gigawatts of capacity annually' once installed (not directly comparable to the 50 GW Investor Day base). Power & Energy is tracking ahead of 2026 capacity growth plans; supply base performing well with no major issues seen.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 3x 2024 large recip capacity; another 15 gigawatts of capacity annually

quarterly_data.signal: Raised 2030 targets: enterprise sales and revenues CAGR now between 6% and 9% from 2024 to 2030; power generation sales target raised to more than 3x sales by 2030 from a 2024 baseline. MP&E capex expected to average 4%-5% of MP&E sales through 2030; positive cash payback on the full reciprocating engine investment expected by the end of the decade.
quarterly_data.figure: CAGR 6% to 9% from 2024 to 2030; power generation sales more than 3x by 2030; MP&E capex 4%-5% of sales

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook raised to low double-digit sales and revenues growth (stronger growth in all three primary segments than January outlook); 2026 capex forecast remains approximately $3.5 billion; MP&E free cash flow now expected above the $9.5 billion of 2025; full-year tariff costs now $2.2 billion-$2.4 billion (vs $2.6 billion prior); adjusted operating margin near the bottom of the target range including tariffs. Power generation growth expected for both reciprocating engines and turbines on data center build-out for cloud computing and generative AI.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 sales growth low double-digit; capex approximately $3.5 billion; tariffs $2.2 billion-$2.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Backup power view (asked about 800 VDC / behind-the-meter displacement risk): CEO says a large part of the base capacity increase is backup power; on current prime power projects 'we're not seeing customers not have backup power', and 'Not every data center is gonna go behind the meter', so backup demand continues; capacity is fungible between backup and prime, and prime/gas compression drives more aftermarket.
